identity.evidence: The published logo file is the Northern Territory Government logo file served from nt.gov.au's own design assets (_design/css/main.css/ntg-logo-mono.svg), referenced as the site's footer logo (img class ntg-logo-footer, alt 'Visit NT.GOV.AU') on the homepage. nt.gov.au refuses automated fetches from this environment (HTTP 403 bot challenge on pages and assets alike), so the bytes were retrieved from the Internet Archive's 2026-11-18 capture of the exact asset URL and SHA-256-verified against that capture (served sha256 1b3e8984304ff377449b91c876ad65bb4c1ac68a24f762029558053f650b7478); the same capture's header carries the same desert-rose device inline (title ntg-desert-rose-reverse), and the device was visually corroborated against the site's apple-touch-icon from the same capture (the orange desert rose). The served file uses CRLF line endings throughout and carries trailing spaces on eleven wrapped lines; the published bytes normalise the line endings to LF and strip the trailing spaces so the copy satisfies the repository whitespace checks — whitespace-only changes, disclosed here; the SVG document is otherwise byte-exact. The mark is the NT Government lockup (desert rose + Northern Territory Government wordmark), a wide mark; the Atlas wide-mark class preserves its proportions. One asset serves both catalogue spellings of the provider name.

rights.evidence: The organisation's own published mark, shown with source and attribution for identification.
